summary: Kyoshun Todo was a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

Kyozo Yamada worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the First Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University, he studied under Sokan Kono, Sogen Asahina, Kanzui Hanamoto, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Sogaku Harada, later heading Sanbo Zen from 1970.

Kyōtarō Nishikawa worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Keio University (circa 1949–1953), he served as Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1990–1997) and at Kanagawa Prefectural Museum (~2002–2012).

Kōgi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1978 to 2004 and was an editor for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).
Kōichi Kozaka is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).

Kōsen Imakita was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Togai Fujisawa, Kyokuso Hirose, Daisetsu Jōen, and Gisan Zenkai. He served as abbot of Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892), and at the Ministry of Religion (~1872–1877).
Kōshō Ōtani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the First Higher School (~1929–1932) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1932–1935).
L. A. Ravi Varma, an Indologist educated at Madras Medical College, served as Honorary Director of the Oriental Manuscripts Department at the University of Kerala from circa 1938 to 1943.

L. P. N. Perera worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a supervisor at the Vidyodaya Campus of the University of Sri Lanka and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti worked in Inner Asian, Sinological, and Tibetan studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University, Eötvös József Collegium, and the University of Paris, he held posts at Eötvös Loránd University from 1931, including chair of Inner Asian Studies from 1940.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshmanacharya, a scholar in Indology and philosophy, held a teaching post at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala in Mathura (attested 1889 and 1900).
Lakshmi Swaminathan was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938). She served as a lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities, he held faculty posts at Gorakhpur (1961–1967), Punjabi University (1971–1981), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1984).
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indologist who served as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Vadodara and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).
Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist who has served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Lama Jampa Thaye is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester and studied under Karma Thinley Rinpoche, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and the 16th Karmapa, later joining the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute faculty.
Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959.

Lama Palden Drolma is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.
